In the United States, the President is the commander-in-chief of the military, as established by Article II, Section 2 of the U.S. Constitution, which states "The President shall be Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States, and of the Militia of the several States, when called into the actual Service of the United States" [d2][d6][d8]. The president is a civilian, not a military official, and holds prime responsibility for the safety and security of the country [d3][d9]. As of January 20, 2025, President Donald J. Trump serves in this role [d7], with the military chain of command flowing from the President to the Secretary of Defense and then to the commanders of the combatant commands [d10]. The President also has the authority to choose or replace commanders in the United States military [d5]. Internationally, the commander-in-chief role is held by different heads of state depending on the country: in Nigeria it is the president, in Norway the monarch, and in Saudi Arabia the king [d1].
